questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's position in the global economy, as cited by the government in January 2026:
1. India became the world's fourth-largest economy by nominal GDP in 2025, overtaking Japan.
2. In purchasing power parity terms, India is the third-largest economy.
3. India overtook Germany in 2025 to become the fourth-largest economy by nominal GDP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India's nominal GDP of about USD 4.18 trillion overtook Japan's, which made it fourth; Germany sits just above India and is projected to be overtaken within roughly 2.5 to 3 years, so 3 is wrong. In PPP terms, which adjust for local price levels, India already ranks third.

questions.q:
The RBI unveiled the Reserve Bank Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It comes into force on 1 July 2026 and replaces the 2021 scheme.
2. Compensation is up to Rs 3 lakh for consequential financial loss and up to Rs 30 lakh for non-financial loss.
3. A complainant can approach the Ombudsman directly, without first approaching the regulated entity.
4. Appeals lie to an RBI Executive Director as the appellate authority.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only 1 and 4 are correct. The limits are the other way round: up to Rs 30 lakh for consequential financial loss and up to Rs 3 lakh for non-financial loss (such as harassment). A customer must first approach the regulated entity and can go to the Ombudsman only after 30 days without a response, and the appeal must be filed within 30 days.

questions.q: The RBI proposed resuming the licensing of new Urban Cooperative Banks after nearly two decades. Which one of the following is correct about the regulation of Urban Cooperative Banks?
o: They are regulated entirely by NABARD, with the RBI having no role in licensing
They are regulated only by State Registrars of Cooperative Societies under State laws
Banking functions such as licensing are regulated by the RBI under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, while registration and management are handled by State Governments or the Central Registrar
They are regulated by the RBI under the Companies Act, 2013 like private sector banks
questions.e: UCBs face dual control: the RBI supervises banking business (licensing falls under Sections 22 and 23 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, as applicable to cooperative banks), while the State Government or Central Registrar covers registration and management. This dual control is why reforms of UCBs involve both the RBI and cooperative authorities. The first urban credit society was founded in Baroda in 1889.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. NITI Aayog's report on MSME schemes proposed converging more than 18 schemes through information convergence and process convergence.
2. The report suggested merging SFURTI with MSE-CDP.
3. SIDBI was set up under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
4. The Union Cabinet approved Rs 5,000 crore of equity infusion into SIDBI over three years to expand MSME credit.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. SIDBI, the apex MSME financing institution, was set up under its own statute, the SIDBI Act, 1989, and is headquartered in Lucknow.

questions.q: A NITI Aayog Trade Watch Quarterly report examined India's trade with its FTA partners in the first quarter of FY2025-26. Which one of the following was among its findings?
o: The trade deficit with FTA partners narrowed, as exports rose 9% while imports fell 10%
The trade deficit with FTA partners rose 59.2% because electronics exports to them collapsed
Exports to ASEAN rose 16.9% and led the growth in exports to FTA partners
The trade deficit with FTA partners rose 59.2%, as exports to them fell 9% while imports rose 10%
questions.e: Exports to FTA partners fell to USD 38.7 billion while imports rose to USD 65.3 billion, which widened the deficit. Electronics exports to FTA partners actually grew 47%, and exports to ASEAN fell by 16.9%. The report is a useful check on the claim that FTAs automatically improve the trade balance.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: A. Committee headed by M.S. Sahoo  B. SAARG Committee headed by Narayan Ramachandran  C. NPS Vatsalya  D. NPS Swasthya Pension Scheme
List-II: 1. Contributory pension scheme for minors with a minimum of Rs 250 a year  2. Framework for assured payouts under the National Pension System  3. Review of the NPS investment framework, including asset allocation and risk governance  4. Pilot under the Regulatory Sandbox integrating health-related benefits with NPS
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The PFRDA's 15-member Sahoo committee designs assured payouts; the nine-member SAARG committee has nine months to modernise the NPS investment framework. NPS Vatsalya serves minors, while NPS Swasthya is a pilot under PFRDA's Regulatory Sandbox Framework.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, 16 Jan 2026; Vajiram & Ravi, 27 and 30 Jan 2026

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the NPS Vatsalya scheme for minors is NOT correct?
o: A minimum contribution of Rs 250 per year is required, with no maximum limit
The account is opened in the minor's name and operated by a guardian
NRIs and OCIs below 18 years are eligible to join
Partial withdrawal of up to 25% of the minor's own contributions is permitted only after the minor attains majority
questions.e: Under the PFRDA guidelines, partial withdrawal of up to 25% of the minor's own contributions is allowed after three years for education, medical treatment or specified disabilities, so it does not wait for majority. The other three statements are accurate.

questions.q:
The Agriculture Minister stated in January 2026 that India's rice production (150.18 million tonnes) exceeded China's (145.28 million tonnes). Consider the following statements:
1. India is now the world's largest rice producer.
2. India supplies only about 10% of global rice exports.
3. Rice is primarily a Kharif crop requiring about 150 cm of rainfall and temperatures of 25-35 degrees Celsius.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India supplies about 40% of global rice exports, with shipments above 20 million tonnes, so 2 is wrong. Rice is sown with the monsoon in the Kharif season and needs high temperatures and heavy rainfall, which is why irrigation fills the gaps in drier States.

questions.q:
Statement-I: India withdrew its import restrictions on low-ash metallurgical coke (ash content below 18%) after the Finance Ministry imposed a provisional anti-dumping duty of USD 60-130 per tonne.
Statement-II: The DGFT had extended the import curbs for 1 January to 30 June 2026 only because no anti-dumping duty was in place.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Quantitative curbs by the DGFT were a stop-gap to protect domestic producers against cheap imports; once the Finance Ministry imposed a provisional anti-dumping duty (on the DGTR's findings), the curbs were no longer needed. Statement-II gives the reason for Statement-I. India imports about 85% of its coking coal.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes:
1. The PLI scheme for White Goods (air conditioners and LED lights) offers 4-6% incentive on incremental sales for five years, with the DPIIT as nodal body.
2. The Advanced Chemistry Cell PLI scheme of the Ministry of Heavy Industries has an outlay of Rs 18,100 crore for 50 GWh of battery cell capacity.
3. Under the ACC PLI scheme, selected firms must achieve domestic value addition of 60% within two years and 25% within five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The value-addition targets are 25% within two years and 60% within five years, so the milestones in 3 are reversed (firms must also invest at least Rs 1,100 crore). The ACC scheme was reported in January 2026 to show a substantial gap between intended and actual outcomes.

questions.q: As per DPIIT data released in January 2026 for April-September 2025, which one of the following is correct?
o: FDI inflows fell 18% to USD 29.8 billion, with the United States the top source
FDI inflows were USD 35.2 billion, up 18% year on year, with Singapore the top source and Maharashtra the top recipient State
FDI inflows rose 18%, with Mauritius the top source and Gujarat the top recipient State
FDI inflows rose 18%, with Singapore the top source and Karnataka the top recipient State
questions.e: H1 FY26 inflows of USD 35.2 billion compare with USD 29.8 billion a year earlier. Singapore (about USD 12 billion) led, followed by the US and Mauritius, and Maharashtra took about 30% of inflows, ahead of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

questions.q:
RBI data showed that outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) fell to a two-year low in November 2025, driven by lower spending on foreign education. Consider the following statements about LRS:
1. It was introduced in 2004 under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
2. It permits resident individuals to remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year.
3. It is also available to resident companies for overseas direct investment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: LRS is for resident individuals, including minors, and covers permitted current or capital account transactions such as education abroad. Companies' overseas investments fall under separate FEMA rules, so 3 is wrong. TCS applies on remittances above Rs 7 lakh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's power sector, as reviewed by the Ministry of Power for 2025:
1. India's installed power capacity reached about 509 GW by November 2025.
2. India reached its NDC target of 50% non-fossil installed capacity in 2025, nearly five years ahead of schedule.
3. The NDC target is 50% of electricity generation from non-fossil sources.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The target under India's updated NDC is 50% cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030, not generation, because generation also depends on weather and plant load factors. India added 55.57 GW of capacity in 2025.

questions.q:
The Government notified coking coal as a Critical and Strategic Mineral in January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It was included in Part D of the First Schedule of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957.
2. India has an estimated 37.37 billion tonnes of coking coal resources, mainly in Jharkhand.
3. India is a net exporter of coking coal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Coking coal is the essential raw material for blast furnace steelmaking, and India is import-dependent (it imports about 85%), so 3 is wrong. Its notification as a critical mineral enables a policy push for domestic production and better beneficiation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Design Linked Incentive (DLI) scheme under the Semicon India Programme:
1. It is implemented by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and offers up to 50% of eligible design expenditure, capped at Rs 15 crore per application.
2. It offers 4-6% of net sales for three years, capped at Rs 30 crore.
3. It had sanctioned 24 chip-design projects as of January 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The sales-linked incentive of 4-6% of net sales runs for five years (capped at Rs 30 crore), not three. The Semicon India Programme has an outlay of Rs 76,000 crore, and the ChipIN Centre at C-DAC supports about 1 lakh engineers and students.

questions.q: The Ministry of Textiles signed MoUs with 15 States for Tex-RAMPS at the National Textile Ministers' Conference in Guwahati. Which one of the following best describes the scheme?
o: A fully centrally funded scheme for FY2025-26 to FY2030-31 giving each State or UT Rs 12 lakh a year and each district Rs 1 lakh a year
A centrally sponsored scheme with a 60:40 Centre-State cost sharing for all States
A PLI scheme giving 4-6% incentive on incremental sales to textile exporters
A credit guarantee scheme for textile MSMEs administered by SIDBI
questions.e: Tex-RAMPS strengthens State-level research, planning and support capacity and is 100% centrally funded, so the States bear none of the cost. It works toward the goal of a USD 350 billion textile industry.

questions.q: NITI Aayog released the Export Preparedness Index 2024 on 14 January 2026. Which one of the following lists the top five Large States?
o: Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Haryana
Karnataka, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana and Kerala
Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh
Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Punjab
questions.e: The Index ranks States and UTs on export readiness using 70 indicators; Uttarakhand topped the Small States category, and Jammu and Kashmir, Nagaland, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, and Goa were the other category leaders. Karnataka, Haryana, Kerala and Telangana do not figure among the top five Large States.

questions.q: The National Statistics Office released the First Advance Estimates of GDP on 7 January 2026, projecting real GDP growth of 7.4% for FY2025-26. Which one of the following bodies is the NSO part of?
o: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.e: The NSO under MoSPI compiles national accounts and releases the advance estimates (real GVA growth 7.3%, nominal GDP growth 8.0%), which are later revised. The Economic Survey, by contrast, is prepared by the Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs under the Chief Economic Adviser.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Economic Survey 2025-26:
1. It put the medium-term potential growth of the Indian economy at about 9%.
2. It was prepared by the Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs under the Chief Economic Adviser.
3. Its estimate of 7.4% real GDP growth for FY2025-26 is the First Advance Estimate, with 6.8-7.2% projected for FY2026-27.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Survey puts potential growth at about 7%, not 9%, and calls India the fastest-growing major economy for the fourth consecutive year. Real growth in 2024-25 was 6.5%.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Economic Survey 2025-26:
1. Average CPI inflation for April-December 2025 was 1.7%, the lowest on record.
2. Private final consumption stood at 61.5% of GDP in 2025-26, the highest since 2011-12.
3. Gross GST collections for April-December 2025 fell 6.7% year on year to Rs 17.4 lakh crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Gross GST collections rose 6.7% year on year to Rs 17.4 lakh crore, so 3 is wrong. The Survey also reported gross NPAs of banks at 2.2% and credit growth of 14.5% in December 2025, and retail inflation of 4.6% in 2024-25 for comparison.

questions.q:
The Economic Survey 2025-26 made the following points. Consider the statements:
1. It set the National Nuclear Energy Mission target at 100 GW of nuclear capacity by 2047.
2. It urged a shift from 'Strategic Indispensability' to 'Strategic Resilience'.
3. It flagged Rs 1.7 lakh crore of unconditional cash transfers as a fiscal risk.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Survey urged the opposite shift, from 'Strategic Resilience' to 'Strategic Indispensability', meaning India should become a country others cannot do without. It also set a target of 5 indigenous Small Modular Reactors by 2033, against current nuclear capacity of 8,780 MW.

questions.q: The Periodic Labour Force Survey for December 2025 reported a labour force participation rate of 56.1% and an unemployment rate of 4.8% (age 15 and above). Which one of the following is consistent with the survey?
o: A worker population ratio of 58.9%, higher than the labour force participation rate
Rural unemployment of 6.7% and urban unemployment of 3.9%
A worker population ratio of 53.4%, with urban unemployment (6.7%) higher than rural (3.9%)
Urban female unemployment of 5.2%, lower than the overall urban rate
questions.e: The worker population ratio is the share of employed persons in the whole population and so must be lower than the labour force participation rate, which also counts the unemployed; 56.1% x (1 - 0.048) gives about 53.4%. The survey put urban female unemployment at 9.1%, above the overall urban rate.

questions.q: The Prime Minister marked a decade of Startup India on National Startup Day, 16 January 2026. Which one of the following is correct about the initiative?
o: Startups are recognised by the Ministry of MSME, and the Fund of Funds is managed by NABARD
Startups are recognised by the DPIIT, and the Fund of Funds is managed by the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund
Startups are recognised by NITI Aayog's Atal Innovation Mission, and the Fund of Funds is managed by SIDBI
Startups are recognised by the DPIIT, and the Rs 10,000 crore Fund of Funds for Startups is managed by SIDBI
questions.e: Startup India was launched on 16 January 2016, and by December 2025 there were over 2 lakh DPIIT-recognised startups and more than 120 unicorns. DPIIT sits in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and recognition under it unlocks tax and compliance benefits.

questions.q:
India's milk production reached 247.87 million tonnes in 2024-25. Consider the following statements:
1. Uttar Pradesh is the largest milk-producing State, with 15.66% of the total.
2. White Revolution 2.0 was launched by the Ministry of Cooperation in September 2024.
3. India has been the world's largest milk producer since 1970, when Operation Flood was launched.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India has been the largest producer only since 1998, almost three decades after Operation Flood was launched on 13 January 1970 by the NDDB under Verghese Kurien, so 3 is wrong. Production rose 3.58% from 239.30 million tonnes in 2023-24.

questions.q:
The Financial Intelligence Unit-India issued guidelines for Virtual Digital Asset service providers. Consider the following statements:
1. Onboarding requires a live selfie with liveness detection.
2. KYC for high-risk clients must be updated only once in five years.
3. Crypto tumblers and mixers are banned and the providers are registered as PMLA reporting entities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: KYC for high-risk clients must be refreshed every six months, so 2 is wrong. Separately, VDA gains attract a 30% flat tax from 1 April 2022 and 1% TDS under Section 194S, and PMLA coverage of VDAs began in March 2023.
